solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make divine covers pong, ironed without the lining being dry

indicators.note: covers means the first piece wraps round what follows it in the clue

parts.note: to make divine is to deify, to treat as a god
pong is British slang for a bad smell, as is hum

indicators.note: taking away the lining leaves just the outside letters of the word ironed

explanation.surface: A strange domestic scene: a god-making ritual masking a smell, with laundry ironed but unlined and drying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures laundry, but 'without the lining' keeps only the outer letters of 'ironed', and 'covers' splits the deifying word around the smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing moisture from air or a room is a way of drying it out.

clue.text: What you could see on TV move across the screen

definitions.text: What you could see on TV
definitions.meaning: ... acts, performers in exaggerated cross-dressing, are a staple of television shows
on a computer you pull an icon over the display with the mouse held down

explanation.surface: A riddle about things that appear on, or travel across, a television screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a cross-dressing performance style and the computing action of pulling an item with the mouse.

clue.text: Told 'Stay hidden'

indicators.note: told means the next words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a stay is a support, so to stay something is to hold it up

explanation.surface: Someone was ordered to remain in hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like part of a command, but it means support (hold up), and 'Told' says that phrase sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lodged in a hiding place, out of sight, is to be concealed or hidden away.

clue.text: After disorder, English strict about protecting monarch's aircraft

indicators.note: after places the English abbreviation behind the word for disorder

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

indicators.note: protecting means the scrambled letters surround and shield the royal abbreviation
about signals that the letters of strict are turned around into a new order

parts.note: HM stands for His or Her Majesty, a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone stern, after some chaos, guards a king's or queen's plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles 'strict' to RSCITT, and 'protecting' wraps it round the royal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Messerschmitt was a German maker of military planes, notably the Bf 109 fighter of the Second World War.

clue.text: Wanting spades not no trumps, one who might propose bridge is to stop

indicators.note: wanting here means desiring, so the card abbreviation is wished in
not marks the bridge-bidding abbreviation as the one pushed out to make room

parts.note: a dentist might suggest a dental bridge to replace missing teeth
NT is the bridge abbreviation for a no-trumps contract
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card-table scene: a bridge player prefers spades to no trumps and is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge vocabulary misleads: the 'bridge' is dental. Replacing NT with S turns DENTIST into DESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean cease or leave off doing something, as in 'cease and desist'.

clue.text: Become confused if upcoming year is productive time

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to addle is to muddle or become confused

explanation.surface: A muddled-sounding thought about whether next year will be a fruitful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reads the first two pieces bottom to top, giving FIELDDA, before the year letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically a day of great activity or success, when everything goes one's way.

clue.text: Favour beginner after swapping tips

indicators.note: swapping the end letters of this four-letter word happens to read it backwards

parts.note: a noob is slang for a newcomer or novice, especially in gaming

explanation.surface: A newcomer asks for help after trading tips with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping tips' exchanges the first and last letters of NOOB; since its middle is OO, that is the same as reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing, a kindness or favour asked or granted.

clue.text: Like gemstone ring left in possession of political activist

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in possession of means the activist holds the letter for left

parts.note: Thomas Paine was the radical pamphleteer of Common Sense and Rights of Man

explanation.surface: A campaigner owns a jewelled ring that was left to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something resembling opal, milky and iridescent.

clue.text: Bug confidently assured to ignore bee's hives

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy or nettle them

indicators.note: to ignore means the letter for bee is left out

parts.note: brash means self-assertive and overconfident
B is the letter whose name sounds like bee

explanation.surface: An insect, cocky and sure of itself, keeps away from the beehives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hives' looks like where bees live, but it is the skin condition urticaria.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives, or urticaria, is an itchy weal-covered skin reaction like that from stinging plants.

clue.text: Sailor overboard presumably rejected navigation aids

indicators.note: rejected means the letters are sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a salt, an old sailor, who has gone overboard is presumably in the sea, so SALT goes inside SEA

explanation.surface: A sailor falls into the sea, presumably having turned down the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT inside SEA gives SESALTA, and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of maps are used to plan and follow a route, so they help with navigation.

clue.text: Competitor chased in races by opponents

indicators.note: by means the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N

indicators.note: in puts the word for chased inside the races abbreviation

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
ran after someone is chased them, so ran means chased here

explanation.surface: A runner is pursued round the course by rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters a race or contest is one of the competitors.

clue.text: Hot buggy, bumpy in motion to the end

indicators.note: buggy, as in full of bugs or faults, signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a bumpy ride is a rough one
going means moving, in motion

explanation.surface: A hot little vehicle bounces along on its way to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a carriage, but it rearranges HOT and ROUGH into THOROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried out completely, all the way through, is done in every detail to the end.

clue.text: Oldest red silk wound in fine threads

indicators.note: wound, as in wound round, means these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: The oldest red silk was spun into delicate threads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as winding thread, fitting the silk, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dressed very smartly and stylishly, in one's finest clothes.

clue.text: Justified the Spanish academic having week up north

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of the grid is north, so the week letter goes first

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
learned means scholarly or academic

explanation.surface: A Spanish scholar spends a week in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserved, merited by effort, is justified.

clue.text: Son on river involved in another display

indicators.note: involved in means the following letters are wrapped inside another river

parts.note: after one river, another is the Exe, which flows through Devon

indicators.note: on means the son letter comes after the river in an across entry

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A boy on a river gets mixed up in a second show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means a second river, EXE, which takes POS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay bare or reveal something to view is to display it.

clue.text: Rebel regrets keeping to degree course in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round so the letters run backwards
keeping means the word for regrets holds the next letters inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so rues means regrets
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree course

explanation.surface: A rebel is sorry about sticking with a university course during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' gives RUETOBAS, which 'in revolution' turns round; 'revolution' fits the rebel surface but only signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel who wrecks or undermines things from within is a saboteur.

clue.text: Unstable land used to shift from mount

indicators.note: unstable means not fixed in place, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Shaky ground was used for getting people off horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from a horse is to dislodge them from their mount.

clue.text: Dislike a mobile with no light

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone does not like a mobile phone without a screen light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone, but it signals the anagram of A NO LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong aversion or hatred is an intense dislike.

clue.text: It enables fit player to get rid of cold — eating stuff up

indicators.note: eating means the trimmed player takes the next letters inside
to get rid of means the cold letter is removed

parts.note: an actor is a stage player
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stuff a cushion is to pad it

explanation.surface: A fit performer shakes off a cold by eating food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of' leaves ATOR and 'up' gives DAP, which 'eating' puts inside. 'fit' looks like healthy but is the verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is a device that lets a plug or part fit something it otherwise would not.

clue.text: Spiky plants caused splits inside of case

indicators.note: splits means the word for caused breaks the middle letters apart and sits between them
inside of means only the inner letters of case are used

parts.note: gave, as in gave rise to, means caused

explanation.surface: Something caused tears in the lining of a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaves are succulent desert plants with stiff, sharp-tipped leaves, so they are spiky.

clue.text: Kind king in row, very upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards
in puts the king letter inside the word for row

parts.note: a row, rhyming with cow, is a loud noise
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gentle king is caught up in an argument and is very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective (gentle) but is the noun, a sort. NOISRE plus V is turned over by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant or particular form of something is one kind or sort of it.

clue.text: Poet's to make weak noodle soup

parts.note: to sap is to drain the strength from, to weaken
pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A poet's way of weakening a bowl of noodle soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Poet stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was an ancient Greek lyric writer from Lesbos.

clue.text: Song's opening covered by support group disheartened boss

indicators.note: covered by means the support group letters enclose the word for opening

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a well-known support group
a way in is an opening or entrance

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the central letter, is taken out

parts.note: a manager is a boss

explanation.surface: A dispirited boss, among a support group, opens with a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle A of MANAGER to leave MANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a popular Christmas carol about the infant Jesus in a stable.

clue.text: Plant found in fair isle

indicators.note: found in means the answer's letters sit inside the run of words fair isle

explanation.surface: A flower grows on a pretty island, or on a Fair Isle jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering garden species with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Far from rubbish journalist's written down

parts.note: far from, as in far from good, means not at all, no
tat is cheap rubbish or junk
ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter's copy, recorded in writing, is far from rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from rubbish' reads as praise but is taken literally, word by word; the 's after journalist stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put in notation, set down in writing or symbols, has been written down.

clue.text: One who feels sympathy burying old actor

indicators.note: burying means the old letter is buried inside the sympathiser

parts.note: a pitier is someone who pities

explanation.surface: A sympathetic mourner buries an elderly actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Poitier was a Bahamian-American film star, the first Black winner of the Best Actor Oscar.

clue.text: Eastern side of European resort where many crash

indicators.note: eastern side means only the right-hand half of the word, as on a map

parts.note: Benidorm is a busy Spanish package-holiday resort on the Costa Blanca

explanation.surface: A part of a European holiday town where lots of people go to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern side' takes the right-hand half, as east is on the right of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash is slang for to sleep, and a dormitory is a shared bedroom for many sleepers.

clue.text: Leaving adobe with no fuss, desires property

indicators.note: with no means the word for fuss is taken out

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing
longings are desires

explanation.surface: Someone moving out of a mud-brick house without fuss wants possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions, the things a person owns, are their property.
